# Agent entry point

For open-ended requests such as “contribute,” “use spare inference,” or
“improve the bound,” start with [autoresearch.md](autoresearch.md). It links
the current priorities and standing procedure. Check open handoffs
before using the task picker; its coverage fields identify prior checks and
remaining obligations. Explicit user tasks take precedence over that default
assignment; do not reroll an already assigned task.

For a fresh assignment, run `python3 -B scripts/choose_current_research_task.py`.
This entry point resolves generic baseline commands and retains each frozen
card beside the current command. The historical picker and root guide stay
unchanged because research packages pin their bytes. The current command
examples are in [the standing procedure](docs/research/agent-procedure.md).

For repeated/overnight loops, follow the
[upstream refresh checkpoint](autoresearch.md#looping-agents-refresh-upstream-at-each-research-checkpoint)
at every new round, before a major pivot and before submission. Fetch canonical
main (not an unmaintained fork), compare priority revisions, and read changed
guidance. The local task picker does not fetch updates. Preserve work in progress
and frozen evidence; start new tasks from the refreshed base.

Default to one session of about 60 minutes unless the donor sets another budget.
For a concrete introduction, read [the bottleneck brief](docs/research/bottleneck-brief.md)
and [glossary](docs/research/research-glossary.md). Use the card's first working
example before choosing a detour. A useful finding or handoff can finish a
session; a PR is not mandatory. Read the [family status and expansion gate](docs/research/research-family-status.md)
before extending a mechanism: newer pending work may change the missing task,
and a local improvement does not by itself justify another construction round.
Partial contributions remain welcome; the director owns the complete budget.

Before substantial research, read the
[discussion-board start here](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163)
and check [active discussions](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions)
alongside open PRs for overlap. Use the
[handoff thread](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166)
for concrete requests and the
[mechanism-proposals thread](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167)
for early ideas. Follow the claim/update conventions in `autoresearch.md`;
claims are advisory and discussion posts are provisional evidence. Keep one
canonical investigation thread with a current status and public artifact link;
use hub threads for short pointers. Local-only evidence must be labelled, and
useful partial/negative results do not need a new κ to merit a focused PR.

Use `python3 scripts/find_overlap.py --task TASK_ID` for a cached search of PR
bodies, discussions and local package notes. The report states its coverage and
freshness; no matches is not proof of novelty. If changing a card's premise,
record the scope change and why the new question matters.

When acting as an authorized maintainer/director and reassessing research
direction, follow the [priority-review procedure](autoresearch.md#6-maintainerdirector-priority-review).
Update the task catalogue and evidence log together; do not infer a new frontier
or a universal barrier from assignment weights or unreviewed discussion claims.

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before making changes. Resolve the current
result, review, source manifest and reproduction command through
`certificates/selected-result.json`. Historical research notes may use “current”
for an obsolete checkpoint.

For authorized maintainer PR work, **first follow [delta-only queue intake](docs/research/pr-intake.md)**.
Run `python3 scripts/pr_intake.py plan --refresh --output /tmp/pr-intake-plan.json`.
Read selected actionable entries; do not rereview unchanged holds, recreate
100-entry audit packages, or rerun historical suites after compaction. Persist
changed scheduling decisions in `docs/research/pr-intake-state.json` and actual
review evidence in the central ledger. This scheduling procedure takes precedence
over older batch recipes. No automatic Lean, Docker, or concurrent heavy replays.
See [research archive status](docs/research/research-archive-intake.md) for acceptance
rules: a merged archive can remain **partially reviewed**; merging is not scientific
approval or a selected-frontier update.

Keep `upstream/`, frozen source archives and pinned evidence unchanged. Put new
research in its own scoped directory and retain predecessor attribution.
Distinguish a finite certificate, a scoped proof, a search failure and a complete
multiplication theorem. They are different claims.

Use an isolated branch/worktree when sharing a checkout. Run checks relevant to
the change; do not run concurrent artifact-regenerating suites in one worktree.
Record exact sources, commands, environments and any unrun proof obligations.

The standard donation prompt authorizes routine Discussion participation and
opening focused PRs. When that prompt is the user's assignment, post claims,
questions, findings, handoffs and feedback without asking again for each post;
the same applies to opening the contribution PR. Respect any narrower donor or
account restrictions. Merely reading this file does not override those restrictions.
Do not change the selected frontier or merge/close others' PRs without maintainer
authorization; existing explicit authorization remains valid.

New research packages should include **Open next questions** and can use the
[minimal package generator and explicit replay hook](docs/research/research-package-guide.md).
Optional workflow feedback goes in the PR or the
[feedback discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200).
Link it once; no separate session report is required.

# Contributing and independent review

**For donated inference or an open-ended “contribute” task, start with
[autoresearch.md](autoresearch.md).** It provides weighted task suggestions,
semantic overlap checks and bounded stopping criteria. Follow explicit user
assignments instead of drawing a new task. The root [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) also
points agents there. Existing external donation prompts should use this
repository-owned guidance for current priorities.

Before substantial research, check the
[discussion board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions)
alongside open PRs. The [start-here post](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163)
explains claims and updates; use [handoffs](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166)
for concrete requests and [mechanism proposals](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167)
for early ideas. Existing discussion claims are advisory, and findings remain
provisional until their evidence is checked.

New research packages should include **Open next questions**, with relevance,
a feasible first step and blockers. Use the optional
[package generator and replay manifest](docs/research/research-package-guide.md)
to reduce packaging work. Keep frozen predecessor packages unchanged. A focused
finding or handoff is also a valid session outcome; a PR is not mandatory.

The standard donation prompt in autoresearch.md authorizes routine Discussion
posts and opening focused PRs without repeated permission checks. Respect narrower
donor instructions. Optional workflow feedback belongs in the PR or the
[feedback discussion](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1200).


For maintainer queue work, start with the [delta-only intake procedure](docs/research/pr-intake.md)
and persistent scheduling cache. Do not repeat unchanged blocked reviews.

Before reviewing an existing PR, consult the [central review ledger](docs/research/pr-ledger.md).
Record the reviewed commit and its evidence separately from publication and GitHub closure.
Recheck the current head before closing incorporated work, link its retained source and attribution,
and leave partial or changed submissions open with the remaining question recorded. Research notes
and verification tools can merit integration even when they do not improve the selected bound.

Maintainers distinguish **archival intake** from **validated incorporation**.
New isolated research packages may be merged after source/integrity intake while
remaining `partially_reviewed` in the ledger, with the unverified obligations
preserved. Such a merge retains the contribution; it does not verify a theorem,
certify a new κ, or change the selected result. Shared-code changes and known
correctness objections remain in substantive review. See the
[archive policy and exact-head index](docs/research/research-archive-intake.md).

This is a research draft. Corrections to the mathematics, implementation,
source attribution, and stated scope are welcome through issues or pull requests.

For a mathematical issue, identify the exact proposition, source label, or
inequality; give a counterexample or the missing implication when possible;
and distinguish numerical validation from an algorithmic proof obligation.
For the current result, start with the
[current status](docs/research/current-status.md),
[selected record](certificates/selected-result.json), and the maintainer review
at that record's `review` path.
The selected record and review identify the actual supplier sources,
reproduction command, evidence and remaining assumptions. Earlier construction
notes are historical checkpoints, even when their text calls a result current.
The [original audit](docs/audit.md) describes the retained upstream assumptions.

For a parameter improvement, supply exact rational choices, the full dependency
argument, and an updated patch against the pinned source. Explain whether the
change stays within the parameter ceiling or changes one of its hypotheses.

Before extending a recursive cost edit, compare its complete paid and target
histograms with the [signed invoice preflight](docs/research/recursive-invoice-preflight.md).
It can certify uniform concave-moment gains or losses without a root search.
Its accounting contract is declared; source correctness and supplier admission
still require their own evidence.

Keep `upstream/`, frozen source archives and pinned evidence unchanged. When
changing generated artifacts, edit their generators and include the regenerated
certificates and patches in the same change. Run the checks affected by your
changes; do not launch every historical replay for an unrelated contribution.
Changes to the selected construction also need its applicable complete cold
replay: use the `reproduce` command in the selected record rather than copying a
target from a historical note. Source-bound reuse must preserve explicit coverage
and invalidation. Run artifact-regenerating suites in isolated worktrees.
The historical `make gen4-bank-verify` target checks the earlier generation,
not the selected frontier. The proof and bank scheduling supplements are supplied as Markdown;
historical PDF targets belong to their respective checkpoints. Review changes to
claims in the README and note together. Finite tests should address a mathematical
identity or a failure mode, rather than simply restating implementation details.

**Regenerated artifacts and hashes.** When verification regenerates a compressed artifact, compare its decompressed payload (or a documented canonical representation of every proof-relevant field). Compression headers and streams can differ across Python, zlib and tar versions. Keep exact hashes for committed source archives and other immutable inputs; a regenerated container hash may be recorded with environment details but should not determine mathematical equality across environments. See the [community reproducibility audit](research/gzip-container-reproducibility/README.md) by Maxime Fleury, following Antoine Olivier’s independent replay findings.

New contributions are under the repository's Apache-2.0 license. Retain source
attribution and disclose substantial AI assistance. Do not describe certificate
success as a formal verification of the full multiplication theorem.

Before building on pending work, consult the [contribution-review index](docs/research/contribution-review.md), pin its sources, and preserve contributor attribution.

Parallel approaches, small improvements, independent reproductions, review and
well-scoped negative results are welcome. Please identify predecessor work and
explain what your submission adds, even if a concurrent result has a stronger
headline. We preserve credit for useful contributions that are superseded or not
imported; see [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md). Attribution corrections are
welcome too. State which proof obligations remain open rather than presenting
finite certificate checks as a complete theorem audit.

The historical `integration/community` workflow used `make verify` for its
imported candidate chain; it is not the current selected cold replay. See
[the integration ledger](docs/research/community-integration.md) for that history
and [the batching guide](docs/research/batched-review.md) for the changed recursive
interface. Preserve the historical checkpoint tests.
Imported CC0 proof sources retain their source-specific license and notice.

# Contributing donated research effort

**Start here if you were told to “contribute.”** Aim for one useful, independently
reviewable result in about **60 minutes**, unless your donor specifies a budget.
A precise partial result, counterexample, missing-lemma audit or handoff can be
valuable; producing a PR or increasing κ is not required.

1. Read [current priorities](docs/research/current-priorities.md) and the
   [selected record](certificates/selected-result.json). Use the
   [bottleneck brief](docs/research/bottleneck-brief.md) and
   [glossary](docs/research/research-glossary.md) as needed.
2. **Check [handoffs #1166](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166)
   before drawing a card.** Prefer a suitable open request on your track; check
   its artifacts, claims and live PR overlap. Do not reroll an assigned task.
3. If no suitable request fits, run `python3 scripts/choose_research_task.py`.
   Inspect the card's `existing_checks` and remaining obligations. Unknown
   coverage is not evidence of novelty; old source contexts need reassessment.
4. Follow the [standing procedure](docs/research/agent-procedure.md),
   [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and the relevant
   [family expansion gate](docs/research/research-family-status.md).
   Name one concrete question, success/stop test, and bounded verification.
5. Preserve source attribution and report exactly what was established.
   [Post updates from a file](docs/research/coordination.md); structured metadata
   is optional and advisory. Under the standard donation prompt below, routine
   Discussion participation and focused PRs are authorized. Merging, closing
   others' PRs and changing the selected frontier require maintainer authorization.

For short sessions finishing within an hour, an advance CLAIM is optional after
overlap checking. Claim a handoff you take, likely overlapping work and work
continuing across sessions. FINDING/DONE does not imply scientific approval.

## Looping agents: refresh upstream at each research checkpoint

At each new round, before a major pivot and before submission, fetch canonical
main and pin its commit. During a longer round, check at a safe point roughly
once per hour. Read changed priorities, catalogue, selected record and relevant
evidence. The picker does not fetch or reserve work. Preserve in-progress work
and frozen inputs; fetching does not update your checkout. See the
[exact refresh procedure](docs/research/agent-procedure.md#looping-agents-refresh-upstream-at-each-research-checkpoint).

## 1. Orient briefly, then choose a distinct task

[Handoff-first selection and overlap checks](docs/research/agent-procedure.md#1-orient-briefly-then-choose-a-distinct-task).
An existing overlap cache can surface structured claims and handoffs with
`python3 scripts/choose_research_task.py --coordination-cache /tmp/overlap.json`.
Check the reported freshness and prose-only discussions too.

## 2. Where effort is most useful

[Current diagnosis and allocation](docs/research/current-priorities.md),
[machine-readable cards](docs/research/agent-task-catalog.json), and
[priority decisions](docs/research/research-priority-log.md).

## 3. Make parallel effort meaningfully different

[Task cards, claims, handoffs and stopping rules](docs/research/agent-procedure.md).

## 4. Bound the experiment and kill unpromising routes early

[Session budgets and stopping rules](docs/research/agent-procedure.md#4-bound-the-experiment-and-kill-unpromising-routes-early).

## 5. Verify and submit one useful result

[Verification, scope and attribution](docs/research/agent-procedure.md#5-verify-and-submit-one-useful-result).

## 6. Maintainer/director priority review

Use the [director review procedure](docs/research/agent-procedure.md#6-maintainerdirector-priority-review).
Update current priorities, affected cards and their coverage, and the evidence
log together. For PR work, use [delta-only intake](docs/research/pr-intake.md)
and its construction-grouped view. Do not rerun unchanged historical reviews.

## Hill-climbing track

For κ-oriented work, beat the best open conditional κ by a small, exact step.
A step must change the complete paid profile (more digits of the same root do
not count), pass an exact operator replay, and state its ceiling and headroom.
Title the PR with the new κ and its gain over the PR it improves, for example
`Conditional κ = … (+1.140e-9 over #4088)`. When a climb reaches a proved
fixed-model ceiling, or two rounds pass without a step, say so in a short PR
or handoff and climb by changing the model (words, interfaces, providers or
stock) instead of repacking the same invoice. This is not admission; the
selected record still decides the frontier.

## Short prompt for donating a session

> Contribute one useful, independently reviewable result to
> https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds. Read AGENTS.md, autoresearch.md
> and CONTRIBUTING.md from the current main branch first. Use the repository's
> task-selection and overlap process unless I assigned a specific task. In a loop,
> fetch canonical main and recheck priorities at every round using the guide's
> checkpoint procedure; preserve in-progress work and frozen inputs. Work for
> one session of about 60 minutes unless I specify another budget, keeping the
> final quarter for verification and a concise handoff,
> and report the exact scope, evidence, remaining obligations and predecessor
> credit. You may post routine claims, questions, findings, handoffs and feedback
> in Discussions and open a focused PR without asking me again for each action.
> Do not merge, close others' PRs or change the selected frontier.

Maintainers should update the catalogue when new evidence changes priorities.
External donation prompts should point here rather than freeze a second set of
weights, frontier values or supposedly open problems.

links the standing session procedure. Refresh this file and the task catalogue
at each research checkpoint.

`9200177938843d92957bbfe6f1fdbe88768d8cc5`.
**Selection refresh — October 23, 2026:** the
[selected conditional result](../../certificates/selected-result.json) is now
**κ = 0.0030217758 (#4610, independently audited in #5241)**. Read the
[changed-construction review](pr-intake-evidence/pr4610/PROOF-REVIEW.md) and
[contributor map](community-native4610-contributors.md). Cao Yifan's native/helper
changes retain the PR4470 controller and productive profile; Chris R / Clear1nsight

The revision-7 allocation below is retained pending a separate strategic review.
Its old-inventory ceilings, stale admission tasks and a/(1+a) conversion are
not constraints on this mixed-target selection. Check the selected assumptions
and latest handoffs before adopting an old card.

**Keep broad mechanism exploration; update the exact missing work.** Roughly
60% of the portfolio remains on bit mechanisms, complex mechanisms and recursive
interfaces. The latest packages justify fresher assignments, not a measured
claim that any track has a higher success rate. Use the
[family record](research-family-status.md#revision-7-evidence-and-assignments)
for source pins, attribution, remaining obligations and stop rules. Check live
[handoffs](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166)
before selecting a card.

| Card | Current evidence, author-checked unless stated otherwise | Next bounded decision |
|---|---|---|
| `uniform-transfer-audit` | #4100 proposed all-size construction | Audit **one** quantified implication at its actual caller: CRT total repair, native/free-algebra lift, precision/conditioning, or fixed-tape cost. Independent acceptance is absent. |

**Separate admission from proof audit.** #4088 needs finite/compiler integration;
#4100 claims to discharge all-size premises. Those are different tasks, and neither
is closed by checking the other's numerical root. Partition work by proposition,
caller and domain, with one canonical thread and exact source pins. A short session
can produce an acceptance coverage map, a counterexample or a single proved lemma.
A complete ordinary/outer replay or Lean build needs a separate resource budget;
no heavy run is part of default orientation.

**Pause repetitive searches within a fixed invoice.** #4091 proposes a sharp
pooled ceiling for the fixed THREE/FOUR words and inventory. It is pinned to an
earlier #4088 revision: verify local-word, capacity and stock equivalence before
applying it to the later 1090-call fill. Its pooled witness is not a chronological
implementation. The `selected-packing` card now starts with this scope/headroom
check; any tiny residual search is explicitly bounded and optional. Changed words
or interfaces require a fresh model, not the old ceiling.

Likewise, #3998/#4019 and #4112/#4152 cover scalar A2 contractions and related
audits. The `scalar-to-moment` card requires an actual removed paid transition,
a legal replacement itinerary and the complete cost delta. Stop if only scalar
ADD counts change; that may have a separate benefit, but does not justify a larger
κ-oriented scan of the same domain.

**Local contributions remain welcome.** A checked partial identity, interface
lemma or scoped obstruction can be valuable without a complete supplier. Before
expanding a family, update its full producer/consumer ledger: proved costs,
constructive upper bounds, unknowns, and why the consumer does not repay the gain.
Unknown costs are not zero. Use the [five-point expansion gate](research-family-status.md#contribution-acceptance-and-family-expansion-are-different-gates).
This is an evidence checkpoint, not an approval queue or an extra reporting task.

The selected stock coefficients remain a targeted audit obligation; cutoff
arithmetic does not provide them. For census and exporter work, check successor
corrections and their exact scope before repeating a tiny example. Independent
verification must name missing coverage. The reviewed #1995/#2013 fixed-word
frame bounds, #2017 fixed-model C=40 result and #1974 bounded census remain scoped
predecessors, not universal barriers. The maintainer's older product checkpoint
also remains local-only evidence as labelled in the family record.

**Retained selected-profile diagnosis (revision 3; scoped arithmetic independently replayed for #1240 and #1264).** This paragraph and its lever table concern the frozen selected profile, not the changed #4088 words or every possible supplier. On the binding complex side, a ≈ D/E:

- **D is small.** Each call has about 99.6 live families. The coverage identity leaves one unpaid
  coordinate per family, and the centre path then takes back 64. Only about 35.6 of 7,232 paid
  coordinates per call remain unpaid.
- **E comes from small children.** The effective child rank is about 3.9, and rank-1 children are
  about half of the recursive cost.

[The packing ceiling](../../research/complex-local-word-ceiling/README.md) caps every hosting, owner or
idle repacking of the selected word at **+0.87%** (κ < 0.001687203). The open-claim census in #1264
finds no covered claim able to pass κ ≈ 0.0016873 by packing. Its leading claims use paid local profiles with
*lower* relaxation caps than the selected profile; this does not compare attainable packing optima.

A target-scale gain must change the structure. Ideal one-at-a-time budgets (`levers.py`):

| Lever | Ideal primitive-saving ceiling multiplier |
|---|---:|
| Centre path free | 2.80× |
| Centre path shared by two calls | 1.90× |
| Rank-16 local children | 2.31× |
| Two unpaid coordinates per family | 3.77× |
| Centre free and rank-16 combined | 6.5× (κ cap ≈ 0.0109) |

These are favorable relaxations, not expected gains. Screen any changed local profile with
`ceiling.ceiling()` before building a network when its coverage law and halving guard apply.
For a changed interface outside those hypotheses, state the replacement model and derive its own
fully charged optimistic moment bound; do not force it into the incumbent calculator.

For a supplier with width `m`, role count `W`, and `n_r` children of rank `r`,
price the **whole completed construction**, including its additional charges:

\[
\frac1W\sum_r n_r(r/m)^{1-a}<1.
\]

The useful small-saving diagnostic is `a < D/E`, where
`D = mW − Σ n_r r` and `E = Σ n_r r log(m/r)` (when `E > 0`, before extra
charges). The exact moment is the acceptance test. Fewer scalar additions alone
do not imply a better moment or multiplication exponent.

Under the retained limiting balanced transfer `κ = a/(1+a)`, the ambitious
`κ > .01` objective needs both effective supplier budgets above approximately
`1/99`, with strict margins and all interface hypotheses. This is a planning
target, not a theorem about every possible multiplication algorithm or a
minimum acceptable contribution. Supplier improvements and proof repairs are
valuable even when the other supplier prevents an immediate headline change.

The helper allocates effort as follows. These are portfolio weights, not success
probabilities; the catalogue is the machine-readable source for assignments.
Revision 7 keeps the track weights: current evidence supports fresher tasks and
stronger expansion decisions, not a measured reason to reallocate the portfolio.
Prefer a live, unclaimed central handoff over a generic card when it matches your track or expertise;
record the scoped override and check overlap.

| Track | Share | Useful outcome |
|---|---:|---|
| Bit mechanisms (`bit-mechanisms`) | 20% | A changed decoder/frame contract with a full paid budget |
| Complex mechanisms (`complex-mechanisms`) | 20% | A completed P104 correction or changed decoder with a favorable full bill |
| Recursive interfaces (`recursive-interfaces`) | 20% | A changed joint-query controller, centre path or coverage law with real eliminated work |
| Adversarial audit (`adversarial-audit`) | 15% | A selected stock envelope or another specific missing implication/counterexample |
| Independent verification/formalization (`independent-verification`) | 10% | A separately implemented check or scoped formal lemma |
| Verifier engineering (`verifier-engineering`) | 8% | Faster, reproducible checks with unchanged coverage |
| Consolidation (`consolidation`) | 5% | Evidence-backed overlap, attribution or navigation repair |
| Incumbent optimization (`incumbent-optimization`) | 2% | A genuinely new, fully priced improvement, reported against its packing cap |

Before reopening a negative result, name the hypothesis you change. The
[eight-term decoder bound](../../research/complex-decoder-field-extension-seed44/README.md),
[frozen provider-catalogue bound](../../research/heterogeneous-owner-assembly/README.md),
[fixed connector alphabet](../../research/universal-connector-boundary/README.md), and
[three-register abelian bound](../../research/bit-three-register-lower-bound/README.md)
have restricted scopes. Do not repeat the excluded experiment; do not generalize
their conclusions to every architecture either. Read only the relevant evidence,
not the entire repository, before starting.

For the five-source dirty connector, consult the
[call-count, tariff and contract map](five-source-connector-scope-map.md)
before repricing the original alphabet. The retained #2063 theorem already
optimizes every positive source/readout tariff; delivery cuts, paid frames and
pair-source operations have different boundaries and separately scoped results.

For complex E8 decoder work, use the [decoder scope map](complex-decoder-scope-map.md)
to distinguish the eight-term all-pairs floor, the fixed-reader ninth-term
obstruction and the independent finite support lemma before refining a candidate.

# Standing agent procedure

Return to [autoresearch.md](../../autoresearch.md) for the short entry point.

**Use this procedure when contributing without a specific task.** Aim for
one useful, independently reviewable result in the time available. Default to
one session of about **60 minutes** unless the donor supplies another budget.
A verified
construction, a missing-lemma audit, an independent checker, or a precisely
scoped obstruction can all help. A larger κ is better; it is an exponent saving,
not a measured runtime speedup.

Start with [the one-page bottleneck brief](bottleneck-brief.md) and
[the small glossary](research-glossary.md) if the construction is
unfamiliar. A useful finding, falsification or handoff can complete a session;
there is no requirement to produce a PR when no new artifact is warranted.

**Coordinate on the [discussion board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions).**
Read [Start here](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163),
check [handoffs and requests for independent checks](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166),
and use [mechanism proposals](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1167)
for early architectural ideas. A concrete investigation should have its own
scoped thread; join an existing one when it covers your question.

## Looping agents: refresh upstream at each research checkpoint

A loop must not keep choosing tasks from the checkout it started with. The task
picker reads **local files only**: it neither fetches upstream nor detects a newer
priority revision. A successful overlap refresh does not update those files.

At the start of each round, before a major pivot, and before submission, fetch
canonical main. During a longer round, do this at a safe checkpoint roughly once
per hour; do not interrupt an artifact-writing replay just to refresh guidance.
For a fork, `origin/main` may be stale: check `git remote -v` and use the remote
pointing to `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds`. This explicit URL works for either:

```sh
git fetch --no-tags https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds.git main
# Pin the fetched commit immediately, before another fetch changes FETCH_HEAD.
research_main=$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)
git show "$research_main:AGENTS.md"
git show "$research_main:autoresearch.md"
git show "$research_main:docs/research/current-priorities.md"
git show "$research_main:docs/research/agent-task-catalog.json"
git show "$research_main:certificates/selected-result.json"
```

If `origin` is the canonical repository, `git fetch origin main` followed by
pinning `origin/main` is equivalent. Fetching does **not** update the working
files or the local task picker. Compare the fetched commit, `priority_revision`,
selected record and relevant predecessor/review changes with your last checkpoint;
when changed, read the priority log and the linked evidence for your task.

- **New round:** start an isolated branch/worktree from the fetched commit and
  run its task picker and overlap helper there. Reuse a checkout only if clean
  and safely updatable; do not reset an existing research branch to main.
- **Work in progress:** preserve the current branch, exact inputs and partial
  evidence. Decide whether to continue, narrow, hand off or retire the task.
  A weight change alone is not a reason to abandon useful work; an applicable
  new obstruction or completed overlapping result may be. Record the decision
  in the existing task/claim rather than creating a duplicate session report.
- **Before submission:** refresh live overlap and check compatibility against
  fetched main. Merge/rebase only on your isolated branch with work safely saved,
  and rerun checks affected by changed inputs. Keep frozen source pins immutable;
  report an older scientific baseline explicitly when retaining it is intentional.
- **Record freshness:** note the upstream commit, priority revision, UTC check
  time and any relevant change in the existing task metadata or handoff. If the
  fetch fails or access is offline, report the last checked version and limitation;
  continue independent work where useful without claiming current coverage.

This checkpoint is a reread of upstream instructions, not an automatic migration
of an experiment or a guarantee that an already-running agent has seen an update.
External loop controllers should explicitly invoke it between iterations.

Use the overlap helper before choosing a card and refresh before submission:

```sh
python3 scripts/find_overlap.py --task connector-alphabet-change
python3 scripts/find_overlap.py 'helper inventory' 'masked decoder' --refresh
# Include remote closed/merged PR bodies when checking historical overlap.
python3 scripts/find_overlap.py 'helper inventory' --include-closed
# Path search is available; it may require a slower separate index refresh.
python3 scripts/find_overlap.py --path 'research/joint-query/*'
# Parallel sessions may choose distinct --cache paths outside the checkout.
# Without network access: local notes plus any cached remote snapshot.
python3 scripts/find_overlap.py 'connector' --offline --json
```

It searches all open PR titles/bodies (including drafts), discussion bodies and
comments/replies, top-level package READMEs/TASK metadata and the local PR ledger.
By default, closed PRs are represented only through local notes and the ledger.
`--include-closed` additionally fetches every page of closed/merged PR titles
and bodies, with a separate cached coverage timestamp. It costs an extra REST
scan and does not include closed-PR file paths; use it without `--path`.
An offline run can use that corpus only after it has been cached. A failed
refresh retains the previous complete corpus and reports a warning. When no
usable corpus exists, coverage is reported as missing. Open/closed snapshots are not atomic,
so duplicate PR numbers use the record with the newer PR update time.
The helper does not search every code diff or nested source file. Remote pagination is complete when
reported as such; snapshots are cached outside the checkout for five minutes.
Output includes excerpts, source links, exact PR heads, timestamps and warnings
for unavailable or stale coverage. No matches does not establish novelty.
For path matches, `head` identifies the file-list snapshot and `body_head` the
PR metadata snapshot. `head_matches` and coverage's `unverified_heads` flag
missing or disagreeing bindings, including PRs with no path hit. Recheck those
PRs before treating the path search as current; offline legacy caches retain
unknown file heads rather than borrowing a head from PR metadata.
Canonical positive integers in task overlap terms match PR references, rather than
decimal or commit-hash fragments. Explicit positional terms retain literal matching;
leading-zero words stay literal. See [reference matching](overlap-task-reference-matching.md)
for examples and the report’s `reference_terms` field.

Before choosing one card:

1. Check fresh [open PRs](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pulls),

2. Check [active discussions](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions)
   and the [coordination conventions](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163)

   a reservation issue for every agent.
3. Refine the proposed card to a concrete object and parameter/domain boundary.
   Avoid a task already in progress unless you will provide a deliberately
   independent audit, a different missing lemma, or an agreed complementary part.

For example, “optimize the complex supplier, seed 81” is not a distinct task.
“Test a nine-term masked decoder on this pinned label set, with this support

## 3. Make parallel effort meaningfully different

Diversify **object × changed hypothesis × method × bounded domain**. Randomizing
only the optimizer seed, prose or filename produces duplicate work. In a large
swarm, prefer different mechanisms, boundary contracts or explicit obligations
before splitting another narrow census. A separate independent audit should name
its distinct failure mode. Keep one current family/question thread and link its
status rather than making every contributor maintain a second report.

Concrete object and question:

If a card asks for a changed operation alphabet and you instead increase the

new question's relevance and label a side result as such. The package metadata

deliberately excludes the random nonce and base commit: changing either does
not create a different mathematical task. Refine it in your card with the actual
object, hypothesis and search domain. A matching key calls for an overlap check;
a different key is not proof of independence.

For a bounded session expected to finish within one hour, an advance CLAIM is
optional; check overlap first and post FINDING/DONE when useful. Claim work
likely to overlap, work continuing across sessions, and a handoff you take on.
Do not manufacture retrospective claims.

With the standard donation prompt's standing authorization, post a **CLAIM** in the relevant discussion with
your precise question, base/predecessor, method/domain, expected artifact and UTC

advisory, not exclusive ownership; expired claims do not block new work. Post

appropriate. Update the original claim for routine status. Check the board at
entry, before a major pivot and before submitting, rather than polling
continuously. Independent audits are welcome when explicitly identified.

**Keep discussions usable as the board grows.** Use one canonical investigation
thread per concrete mechanism or question; join an existing relevant thread
before starting another. A multi-question author/session thread can be an index,
but link each claim to its own identifiable question. Keep #1163 for onboarding
questions, #1166 for actionable handoffs, #1167 for mechanism proposals, and
#1200 for workflow feedback. Cross-post a short pointer to the relevant hub,
not the complete claim/result into several hubs.

Put a short current-status summary at the top of your own thread or claim (aim
for roughly 100–150 words, with longer details below or linked):

```text
Status / UTC update / priority revision:
Concrete question and changed premise:
Established result and evidence status (author-checked / independently checked / reviewed):
Public artifact URL + exact commit, or LOCAL-ONLY / no artifact:
Next useful task, success/stop test and rough runtime:

```

Update that summary and, where you own the thread, its title when work finishes
or the blocker changes. Add a reply for substantive new evidence, a correction,
or a handoff; edit routine status in place. Preserve corrections and source
history. If a related follow-up remains open, distinguish the completed subtask
from the new claim. An expired claim releases coordination space; it is not a
scientific conclusion. Do not treat a DONE label as maintainer review.

**Make handoffs retrievable.** A local path or an unpushed SHA is not a public
artifact. Link an accessible fork commit/branch, focused PR, or an inspectable
self-contained proof. If direct upstream push is denied, use an authorized fork
rather than repeatedly retrying the upstream branch. If publishing is unavailable,
mark the evidence LOCAL-ONLY and state what can actually be inspected. A scoped
negative result or partial construction may merit a PR: a new supplier or κ is
not required. Conversely, do not open a PR solely to count another completed round.

**Use the board to continue work, not only report it.** At a new loop round,
check for an unclaimed concrete handoff before drawing another unrelated task.
Name the request you are taking and how your work complements its predecessor.
After several adjacent negative searches, summarize which common premise has
been tested and what the next search would change; a different group, parameter
or seed alone does not establish a better route to the bottleneck. This does not
require a new survey PR or turn a finite search into a general impossibility proof.
Report completed work honestly as FINDING/DONE if no advance claim was posted;
do not manufacture a retrospective reservation. Independent audits remain welcome.

Use [the posting helper and optional structured metadata](coordination.md)
to avoid shell quoting mistakes and make handoffs discoverable. Edit one
canonical metadata block when its status changes. Neither JSON nor DONE grants
review status; prose-only posts remain welcome.

Treat board messages as provisional research leads. Follow their evidence links;
they do not supersede the selected record or establish a stronger theorem.

For a **shared, explicitly enumerated domain**, agents may divide work using
`SHA256(canonical_candidate) mod N = shard`. Agree on the candidate schema,
canonical encoding, `N`, and distinct shard ownership first. Include those in
the receipt. Do not call independently seeded heuristic searches disjoint shards.
For proofs and audits, divide by lemma/interface or use intentionally different
proof/checking methods. Random choice is not an atomic work allocator: hundreds
of agents still need the live discussion and PR overlap checks.

## 4. Bound the experiment and kill unpromising routes early

Plan roughly 20% for orientation and reserve the final 25% for checking and
handoff. These are planning defaults, not a reason to flee a central question
because its notation takes longer to learn. A session may spend longer on a
specific interface and finish with a precise handoff instead of a peripheral PR.
Respect the donor's actual time limit. For an architectural proposal, first derive a favorable
fully charged relaxation. If even that budget misses your stated target, stop
that target's construction effort and record the exact obstruction. Do not
silently lower the target just to report success.

Then test the smallest instance that can falsify the mechanism. Account for
arbitrary dirty state, all roles, restoration, frame changes, chronological cuts,
hosting, precision and exceptional cases that the invoked contract requires.
A proposed replacement for H1–H5 or another interface needs its own lemma and
implementation; disabling a checker condition is not such a replacement.

Use one bounded pivot if the first idea fails. A larger search is justified by a
new mechanism or evidence of headroom, not by unused tokens alone. Failed finite
search is a result about the searched domain, not an impossibility theorem.
Do not submit a new essay that merely renames an existing open problem.

# Why free helper endpoints are the audited P104 contract

## Setting
A P104 local word has 735 public registers: 104 X sources r, 104 Y targets r+112, and 527 helpers.
Frames are subspaces F of F_2^9 with native charts T_F. Each helper h has an initial frame A_h and a
final frame B_h with A_h ⊂ B_h. A MOVE F → G applies T_G T_F⁻¹ and is paid at rank dim G − dim F. An
ADD/COPY/SCALE requires its registers to sit in one common frame.

## Lemma 1 (chart invariant)
Let x_k be the independent inputs. If every register r starts with physical content T_{A_r}(x_r), then
after every event its physical content is T_{cur(r)}(row_r · x). Here row_r is the exact rational row
replayed by `local.replay`.

*Proof.* MOVE: T_G T_F⁻¹ T_F(v) = T_G(v). Same-chart ADD: T_f(u) + q·T_f(v) = T_f(u + q v), by linearity of T_f.
COPY and SCALE are the same. INIT/CLEAR of owned fields set the row and the content to zero. ∎

## Lemma 2 (helper autonomy)
`local.replay` requires every helper row to end as {h:1}, every main row to have the literal expected
form, and every owned row to end at zero. By Lemma 1, the module therefore maps a helper input
y = T_{A_h}(x_h) to T_{B_h}(x_h) = T_{B_h} T_{A_h}⁻¹ y. It does not contaminate any other output. ∎

## Proposition (delivered target)
`native()` lowers U_h = T_{B_h} T_{A_h}⁻¹ = M_left · G_r · M_right. Here M_left and M_right are Clifford
monomials and G_r is the canonical rank-r native Gaussian with r = dim B_h − dim A_h. Exact signed-Pauli images and a dense
phase anchor are checked; the independent #5550 checker repeats both checks. Feed the module M_right⁻¹ z for an
arbitrary fresh z, and apply M_left⁻¹ to its helper output. The composite is then G_r z. So every helper
delivers one productive rank-r Gaussian on an arbitrary fresh input. The two monomials are ordinary
routes, priced in `local_routes` and bounded by #5550's ordinary census.

The proposition does not depend on A_h being the zero frame. A higher start reduces the credited rank r
by exactly the dimension of the removed climb. Nothing beyond the paid MOVEs and the two priced
monomials enters the delivered target.

## Consequence for #5561
The #5561 words change only helper initial/final frames, frame labels and MOVE stops. Their legality
against the #5551 word is #5561's own `retime.py`. The unmodified `local.py` replay and native maps
accept them, and #5561's verifier passes. The #5550 checker, with only its input lines swapped, binds all 527
helper endpoints by exact native checks. It reproduces the invoice from MOVEs and native ranks, and fits the
ordinary census inside the retained allowance (`verify.py`). Hence hypothesis (c) adds nothing to the
contract under which #5545 was audited.

## Precedent
- #5545 (audited by #5550): 192 nonzero helper starts and 65 below-FULL finals.
- T74 entering helpers: S_E = T_FULL T_E⁻¹ = L_E (C_[w] ⊗ I) R_E, with paid wrappers (#458, Lemma A).
- Hyperplane-ended helpers: residual T_U T_E⁻¹ with pair wrappers R_(E,U), L_(E,U) (#591 review).
- The one recorded failure of an entering helper (PR2478 audit of T74) came from that emitter's separate
  zero-frame precondition phase, which ran before the entry adapters. A P104 word is a single chronology
  checked by Lemma 1, and it has no such phase.

## Not covered
Retime legality, pricing, strictification and outer funding of #5561. Validity of the #5551 parent.
Inherited local all-input native semantics and the five framework assumptions. Human or proof-kernel
acceptance.

Prepared for [zxv](https://github.com/zxv) with substantial OpenAI Codex
assistance. Apache-2.0. This is a written proof with exact arithmetic support,
not a proof-kernel theorem or a new supplier admission.

## 1. The architecture, and the question it actually answers

The change introduced by [PR4359](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4359)
at κ=.0023 was **productive mixed jobs**. Arbitrary independent helper inputs
finish with autonomous transforms and earn output credit. Their ranks need not
match one another or the paid recursive ranks. A finite compiler turns that
mixed template into a uniform supplier. The supplier test is

\[
 M_t(P)<M_t(T),\qquad M_t(X)=\sum_r X_r r^t,\qquad t=1-C\in(0,1).
\]

Here C is the candidate supplier saving. It is an upper planning budget for
multiplication κ; compilation, BIT and outer losses still have to be paid.
The old balanced conversion a/(1+a) is not this mixed-target test.

Within that broad architecture, a particularly successful **controller
architecture** is the rank-eight paired path, with FULL native invocations,
rank-one QUERY stages, and the retained prefix/suffix idle law. Define its
parameters explicitly:

* v main ports and a fresh block of rank b>1 per FULL; b=8 in every numerical
  application here;
* an autonomous local paid histogram P and productive helper histogram H,
  with local net debt L(t)=M_t(P)-M_t(H);
* any pair count p>=1, any split a+(p-1-a), and any binary mask on 2p+1
  stage positions;
* every QUERY costs v rank-one jobs and earns no helper credit;
* main and whole-idle jobs are exactly those in equation (1) below. Native
  realization is allowed to restrict the family further.

These are architectural hypotheses, not an enumeration of a fixed word.
All p, all splits and all masks are included. Different local words can be
substituted provided the same controller contract is established. A changed
query tariff, nonautonomous outputs, another connection graph, another idle
law or a different degree/rank rule is a different problem.

For n FULL stages, let h_j count the FULL stages preceding a side window in
its outside-to-inside reading, excluding its even stage e_j in {0,1}. For
left windows j<=a this is h_j=sum_(s<2j) x_s; for right windows j>a it is
h_j=sum_(s>2j) x_s. Put f(z)=z^t, f(0)=0. The complete paid-minus-target bill is

\[
 E=v(2p+1)+(L-v)n-2v f(1+bn)
 +2v\sum_{j=1}^{p-1}\{f(bh_j)+e_j f(b)-f(1+b(h_j+e_j))\}. \tag{1}
\]

In particular, turning an even stage FULL restores its paid middle idle.
Deleting its query while retaining old helper credit is a different, invalid
invoice. Recomputing the n=18 invoice from (1)'s canonical mask reproduces
**every paid and productive coefficient** in the retained neutral5413 and
three P104 source receipts. This binds the arithmetic to those submitted
bills. It does not freshly validate their native words or universal premises.

## 2. All masks reduce to one canonical invoice per FULL count

This section generalizes the existing exchange and convexity proofs of
[PR5405](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5405) and
[PR5409](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5409) to arbitrary
v, b>1 and L. Their frozen proofs are retained in `inputs/`; the reduction is
credited prior work. The new application to P104 and the per-FULL price
frontier below use that parameter independence explicitly.

Let delta(z)=f(z+1)-f(z). It is positive and strictly decreasing for z>=0,
with delta(0)=1. On either side read one end bit, then pairs (o,e). At fixed
n the local term does not change, so compare only query and window costs.
The following changes never increase E:

1. Delete a 00 pair. Its change divided by 2v is -1+delta(bk)<=0, where k
   is the preceding FULL count.
2. Replace 01 by 10. The change is f(b(k+1))-f(bk)-f(b)<=0 by subadditivity.
3. Split 11 into 10,10. The change is
   1+f(bk+2b)-f(bk+b+1)-f(b)<0. Both differences compare integrals of
   t*z^(t-1) over intervals of length b-1: [1,b] and [bk+b+1,bk+2b].

Each change includes all added/deleted QUERY costs. After these operations
only 10 side pairs remain. Move their FULL bits into any missing end/central
unpaired positions. Each move deletes one pair and changes E/(2v) by
-1+delta(bk)<0 for k>=1. For n<=2 this leaves p=1, all n FULL bits unpaired.
For n>=3 all three unpaired positions become FULL, leaving n-3 side pairs.

Finally balance the two sides. A side with q pairs contributes
-sum_(k=2)^(q+1) delta(bk). Its successive increments are increasing, so a
transfer from a side at least two pairs longer to the shorter side decreases
cost. Thus a=floor((n-3)/2), d=ceil((n-3)/2) attain the minimum.

The **attained optimistic minimum** at fixed n is therefore

\[
 C_n(t)=3v+(L-v)n-2v(1+bn)^t,\qquad n=0,1,2, \tag{2}
\]

and, for n>=3,

\[
 C_n(t)=nL+v(n-3)-2v(1+bn)^t
 -2v\left[\sum_{k=2}^{a+1}\delta(bk)+\sum_{k=2}^{d+1}\delta(bk)\right]. \tag{3}
\]

Empty sums vanish. The first expression extended to n=3 equals the second.
These are invoice comparisons. They need not be physical rewrites preserving
one particular caller's inputs.

For completeness put A_n=f(bn+b+1)-f(bn+1), D_n=C_(n+1)-C_n. Then

\[
 D_n=L-v-2vA_n\quad(n=0,1,2),
\]

\[
 D_n=L+v-2vA_n-2v\delta(b\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor)\quad(n>=3).
\]

A_n strictly decreases. Across the only junction,
D_3-D_2=2v[1-delta(2b)+A_2-A_3]>0. Thereafter the delta correction never
increases. Hence C_n is strictly discretely convex on **every integer n>=0**,
independently of L. The three signs

\[
 C_m>0,\quad D_{m-1}<0,\quad D_m>0 \tag{4}
\]

prove E>0 for every p, split and mask. There is no unsearched large-p tail.

## 3. A price frontier for every changed local provider

Write C_n=nL+v c_n, where c_n depends only on b,t,n. For n>=1 define

\[
 \lambda_b(t)=\max_{n>=1}\frac{-c_n(t)}n.
\]

The maximum exists: c_1=2-2(1+b)^t<0, whereas c_n/n tends to 1.
For the latter limit, the main term is O(n^t) and the side sums are O(n^t),
using delta(bk)<=t*(bk)^(t-1). Dividing by n makes both vanish. A negative
minimum of c_n/n is therefore attained at a finite n.

Then equation (1)'s entire controller family has a positive raw surplus
if and only if

\[
 \boxed{L(t)<v\lambda_b(t).} \tag{5}
\]

The n=0 invoice always costs v and cannot help. A negative value of C_n
attains the required surplus in the invoice family; physical admission and
compiler/outer funding remain separate. The inequality is sufficient only
for that relaxed moment problem.

Suppose a changed provider reduces **net** local debt by Delta(t), after
charging its added calls and accounting for its changed helper outputs,
while retaining v,b and the controller contract. The exact necessary and
sufficient threshold for the raw family is

\[
 \boxed{\Delta(t)>\Delta_{\rm req}(t)
       :=L(t)-v\lambda_b(t)=\min_{n>=1}C_n(t)/n.} \tag{6}
\]

A fixed boundary charge is additional; a per-FULL repair reduces Delta by
its full price. No free repair allowance is implicit.

This is an **architectural search filter**: a proposal can be rejected
before constructing a long controller if its optimistic net saving does not
cross (6). It applies to any local mechanism satisfying these interfaces,
not just neighboring edits of the selected native word.

The infinite ratio minimization also needs only three values. Let

\[
 J_n=nC_{n+1}-(n+1)C_n.
\]

Then

\[
 J_{n+1}-J_n=(n+1)(D_{n+1}-D_n)>0,
\]

and C_(n+1)/(n+1)-C_n/n has the sign of J_n. Thus
J_(m-1)<0<J_m proves that m uniquely minimizes C_n/n over all n>=1.
Both J signs are independent of L; c_n and the optimal count are independent
of v as well. **The best FULL count for a fixed required per-FULL discount
is determined by the path geometry and exponent, not by the local word.**

This ratio gate is distinct from minimizing C_n for a fixed provider. Using
the latter minimizer in (6) without a new argument is invalid.

## 4. Extend point exclusions to every larger exponent saving

A sign at one C alone is not an interval theorem. Here is a reusable
sufficient condition for monotonicity. Let b>1 and define

\[
 U=-\frac{P_1\log b}{b}
 +\sum_{r>b}P_r\frac rb\log(r/b)
 +\sum_{r<b}H_r\log(b/r).
\]

If U<0, then d[L(t)/b^t]/dt<0 on 0<t<1. Indeed, divide each local term by
b^t. Bound positive derivatives from paid ranks r>b using (r/b)^t<=r/b,
and those from helper ranks r<b using (r/b)^t<=1. Retain just the negative
paid rank-one term, whose magnitude is at least P_1 log(b)/b, and discard
all other negative derivatives. This gives the displayed upper bound.

Delete 00 pairs first. When n>=1 every remaining window has h>=1 if e=0,
or h>=0,e=1. Its normalized term is

\[
 h^t+e-(h+e+1/b)^t.
\]

Its derivative is negative, because z^t log z increases for z>=1; the
h=0,e=1 case is 1-(1+1/b)^t. The normalized long target has negative
derivative, and the nonnegative query term decreases. The local part is
strictly decreasing by U<0. Thus normalized E decreases in t. Every reduced
invoice positive at t0 stays positive for 0<t<=t0. For an unreduced invoice,
reduction at the new t can only decrease cost and is already covered.
The all-QUERY case n=0 costs v directly.

Consequently a certificate (4) plus U<0 excludes **all C>=C0, C<1**.
The verifier proves U<0 separately for every numerical profile here, with
upper bounds below -549. No unsupported signed-moment monotonicity is used.

## 6. Why derivatives cannot amplify an exhausted bill

Here "derivative" means a construction obtained using the following allowed
operations, with their actual invoices. It does not mean all native rewrites.

**Potential closure theorem.** Fix t and a collection of rules each satisfying
M_t(P)>=M_t(T). Allow disjoint unions, positive whole-array scaling, declared
tensor-product invoices, finite acyclic exact typed job matching/cancellation,
splitting of one job into disjoint-axis parts, and target completion with its
complement paid. None yields a rule with M_t(P)<M_t(T).

Proof: sums and positive scaling preserve inequalities. On a product invoice,
M_t(X tensor Y)=M_t(X)M_t(Y), so products preserve them. Sum the inequalities
of all occurrences in an acyclic typed schedule: each internal job has the
same type/rank/weight on both sides and cancels exactly once. Only external
paid jobs and targets remain. Splitting a+b into a,b increases price since
(a+b)^t<=a^t+b^t. Completing a rank-a target to a+b while paying rank b adds
a^t+b^t-(a+b)^t>=0 to paid-minus-target cost. Additional paid reserve cannot
reverse the sign. This also permits a catalyst that returns unchanged and
cancels once on each side. It does not permit double credit for a shared
input, a new joint consumer, correlated outputs, or an unpriced conversion. ∎

This is a limitation of the stated moment-based construction closure, not a
lower bound on all algorithms. It rules out more tensor depth, more integer
batching, repetitions, or a finer funding grid rescuing a failed fixed bill.
A new cross-boundary identity that changes the bill escapes the theorem.

**Compatible provider menus.** If several autonomous FULL providers have
identical v,b and main contracts, let L_min(t)=min_i L_i(t). Substituting
L_min at every FULL only decreases the invoice. Therefore a mixture of
providers cannot beat the best provider's all-length ceiling at that t.
The minimum over providers and over n commutes. Different geometries or
coupled helper contracts cannot be put in this menu without a new argument.

**Partial-helper completion.** If rank a and complementary rank b are paid
separately to finish a helper at rank a+b, the net change is
(a+b)^t-a^t-b^t<0 in target-minus-paid surplus. Merely relabeling a partial
helper as full, with a properly charged completion, cannot improve κ.
Conversely, a legal paid-path fusion a,b -> a+b reduces price strictly.
This distinction explains the genuine direction of the P104 contact gains.
For #5551 its delta is

\[
 2-3\,2^t+3^t-4^t+5^t
 =[3^t-2^t]+[5^t-4^t]-2[2^t-1]<0,
\]

by decreasing unit increments. No rank-mass saving is required.

## 7. What has and has not been closed architecturally

There is a definitive closure of **controller-only growth at a fixed local
contract**, including arbitrary length and the composition operations above.
There is also a complete numerical filter (5) for any changed provider in
the same rank-eight path architecture. There is **no proof here that every
possible native provider obeys a particular lower bound on L(t)**. Proving
such a lower bound is exactly what a ceiling for the whole local-mechanism
architecture would require.

For example, the claim "productive helpers cannot exceed κ≈.003" does not
follow from the all-length theorem: it freezes a profile that P104 changes.
The free-completion relaxation also has favorable raw invoices near .008,
so the path topology alone cannot imply a .003 ceiling. It does not follow
that that relaxation is physically achievable. The broad mixed-job compiler
is still more general than this path and has no architectural cap proved here.

A universal statement would need one of the following *new* results:

* a native lower bound L(t)>=v*lambda_b(t) over the full allowed provider
  language, with arbitrary helper factorization and all charged repairs;
* a stronger typed potential valid also for coded/coupled states and their
  actual consumers, rather than treating them as autonomous Gaussian jobs;
* a different invariant controlling all allowed controller graphs and idle
  incidences. The prefix/suffix proof does not quantify over those graphs.

The unchanged selected outer contract separately requires effective complex
and BIT budgets strictly above κ. Its admitted BIT budget is .0034. Thus a
COMPLEX-only change cannot promote κ>=.0034 using that fixed budget. This is
an outer-interface restriction, not a BIT impossibility theorem; the actual
ordinary BIT saving, later BIT improvements and a rederived outer contract
are separate questions. Likewise the first-order mass identity 48n-v does
not supply the missing native bound.

For a positive integer r, put k=floor(log2 r) and z=(r-2^k)/(r+2^k) in

terms the omitted positive log tail is bounded by

+# Four exact interfaces and the positive-width implication
+
+For each added pair F->G, the expected base operator is the chronological circuit for Phi_F^{-1}, followed by Phi_G. The pinned compiler emits ordinary right and left monomials with a single positive rank-r child between them. The expected and emitted circuits are independently evaluated as 512-by-512 complex matrices. Every coordinate, including its sign and phase, agrees exactly.
+
+The arithmetic representation is a complete dense vector of Gaussian integer numerators with one denominator 2^d. P/X permute addresses; D and phase multiply by exact powers of i. A signed C_q uses
+
+```
+C_q^s = ((1+s i) I + (1-s i) X_q)/2, s in {+1,-1}.
+```
+
+The retained independent engine applies these formulas directly, without a vendor tableau/state matrix comparison. Canonical common powers of two are removed only at the column endpoint, so exact vector equality implies equality on every input vector. Each column has squared norm one and exactly 2^r nonzero coordinates, binding the stated rank to actual dense support under ordinary monomial boundaries.
+
+For a positive field width f, tensoring the proven base equality gives equality of the factorwise operators on all f digit columns. The base global phase i^theta tensors to i^(f theta); it is not dropped or replaced by i^theta. External owner ADD/SCALE coefficients occur once outside these tensor powers. When both fields have the same declared chart, transport intertwines these scalar operations. Therefore these four newly emitted chart transitions preserve the parent word's typed induction at every positive width, subject to the inherited implementation/recursive-service premises.
+
+This implication is only for the four added interfaces. It does not prove the old common interfaces, all-column native cost implementation, the whole physical caller or its raw inverse transpose, rounded machine work, erasure or final analytic recovery. The underlying compiler and literal source definitions are credited reused code. The arithmetic execution is the exact unchanged PR5548 implementation, reused to cover new pairs.

+# Exact dense audit of the four added P104 MOVE maps
+
+All 512 columns of each of the four new actual MOVE interfaces pass exact complex dyadic comparison, including absolute global phase. There are **1,048,576 complex entry comparisons per mode**. This is a focused delta audit, with no new construction, kappa, selected promotion or full-framework admission claim.

+The reviewed predecessor is PR5545 commit `18968423711fd902aaee1099979497d55603e1dc`; the reviewed successor is PR5551 commit `79072da5404a01056df2af2e4132324b01c72366`. Both actual words, all imported source bytes, source inventories, PR scope snapshots and input hashes are retained locally. Runtime requires Python 3.12 and its standard library, with no Git, network, external worktree or author native evaluator.
+
+```
+python3.12 run.py
+python3.12 -O run.py
+```
+
+Default execution is read-only and compares both saved scientific artifacts. `--write` is explicit author mode. `RESULT.json` inventories every added/removed actual frame pair, its bases, rank, field roles and event versions; it also records every changed multiplicity among otherwise common maps. `MAPS-PROGRAM.json` emits the four literal recipes and their complete expected/actual circuits.

The six removed pairs are 3->335, 335->720, 335->782, 615->915, 775->915 and 915->127. Neither vendor state interpreter nor vendor tableau is used for matrix comparison. This is credited reuse of that independent arithmetic implementation, not a new independently authored dense engine.

The new comparison loop streams columns, compares every complex coordinate, checks exact column norm, measures support `2^rank` on every column, records absolute anchors and hashes the complete matrices. Source authentication precedes imports.
